label: GitHub
description: Read repositories and code, and open, comment on, and update issues and pull requests as your own GitHub account.
securityDescription: GitHub sign-in opens through Composio and acts as the connected person's own GitHub account, separately from Chickpea's Repositories feature. Agents can read the repositories, code, issues, pull requests, and checks that account can reach. With write access, Agents can open, edit, label, comment on, close, and reopen issues, and open, close, reopen, and mark pull requests ready for review. Agents cannot push code, create branches or repositories, merge or approve pull requests, request reviewers, assign issues, publish releases, run workflows, read secret scanning alerts, delete anything, or change repository settings, collaborators, branch protection, secrets, webhooks, or visibility.

drop.GITHUB_CREATE_REPOSITORY: With private withheld, GitHub creates a public repository.
drop.GITHUB_LIST_SECRET_SCANNING_ALERTS_FOR_A: Alerts carry the leaked secret values, which stay out of model context.

capabilities.description: Creates a pull request in a GitHub repository, requiring existing `base` and `head` branches; `title` or `issue` must be provided.

base.description: The name of the branch you want the changes pulled into. This must be an existing branch on the current (target) repository. You cannot submit a pull request to one repository that requests a merge to a base branch of another repository.

body.description: The detailed description or contents of the pull request.

head.description: The name of the branch where your changes are implemented. IMPORTANT: This branch must already exist in the repository (or fork) before calling this action. You must first create the branch and push commits to it (using git or the 'Create a reference' action), then create the PR. For cross-repository pull requests, namespace `head` with the source owner and branch, like `username:branch`.

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case-sensitive.

draft.description: Indicates whether the pull request should be created as a draft. Draft pull requests cannot be merged until marked as ready for review.

issue.description: The number of an existing issue in the repository to convert into a pull request. If provided, the issue's title and body may be used for the pull request. Required if `title` is not specified.

owner.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case-sensitive.

title.description: The title of the new pull request. Required unless `issue` is specified.

head_repo.description: The name of the repository (e.g., 'octocat/Hello-World') where the changes in the pull request were made. This field is required for cross-repository pull requests if both the source and target repositories are owned by the same organization but are different repositories.

maintainer_can_modify.description: Indicates whether maintainers of the upstream repository can modify the pull request. This is primarily relevant for pull requests originating from forks.

capabilities.description: Primary tool to find and search pull requests. Supports filtering by repository, author, state, labels, and merge status, and returns structured PR data for reliable use in workflows. GitHub search results are capped at ~1000 total items; narrow filters when totals approach this limit. `created_since`/`updated_since` filter on creation/update timestamps, not `merged_at`; apply merge-date filtering client-side.

page.description: Page number of results to fetch.

repo.description: Filter by specific repository. Can be provided in 'owner/repo' format (e.g., 'facebook/react'), or as just the repo name when used with the owner parameter. When owner and repo are both provided and have the same value, they are combined as 'owner/repo'. When omitted along with owner, search scope is determined by for_authenticated_user flag. The repository must exist and be accessible with your token.

sort.description: Field to sort results by. Set explicitly to 'updated' with `order=desc` when recency matters; default behavior may return best-match relevance ordering instead.

owner.description: Filter by repository owner (user or organization). Can be used alone to search all repositories for an owner, or combined with repo parameter to specify owner and repo separately. When both owner and repo are provided, the search is scoped to 'owner/repo'. When omitted along with repo, search scope is determined by for_authenticated_user flag. The owner must exist and repositories must be accessible with your token.

query.description: Optional search query for PR title, description, or commit messages. Supports GitHub search syntax including label filters (e.g., 'label:bug'), logical operators (AND, OR, NOT), and text search. If not provided, PRs will be listed based on other filter parameters. Type qualifiers (type:pr, is:pr, is:issue, type:issue) are automatically normalized. When using logical operators with qualifiers like labels, the query is automatically grouped for proper parsing.

author.description: Filter by PR author username. Must be a valid GitHub username (alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, cannot start or end with hyphen). No dots or other special characters allowed.

assignee.description: Filter by PR assignee username. Use '@me' for current user. Must be a valid GitHub username (alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, cannot start or end with hyphen). No dots or other special characters allowed.

mentions.description: Filter by username mentioned in PR. Must be a valid GitHub username (alphanumeric characters and hyphens only, cannot start or end with hyphen). No dots or other special characters allowed.

per_page.description: Number of results per page (maximum 100). GitHub caps total search results at ~1000 items; iterate `page` until results fewer than `per_page` are returned, and add `repo`, `label`, or date filters when totals approach 1000.

is_merged.description: Filter by merge status. True for merged PRs, False for unmerged, None for all.

created_since.description: Filter PRs created after this date (ISO 8601 format). Provide as UTC ISO 8601 timestamp to avoid off-by-one-day errors at range boundaries. Does not filter on `merged_at`.

updated_since.description: Filter PRs updated after this date (ISO 8601 format).

response_detail.description: Level of detail in the response. 'minimal' (default) returns an optimized response for AI agents. 'full' returns the complete GitHub API response.

for_authenticated_user.description: Include private repositories accessible to the authenticated user in search results. When True without repo/owner, searches PRs involving you (author, assignee, mentions, commenter) across all accessible repos. When False without repo/owner, restricts to public repos only. When repo/owner is specified, this flag has no effect on scope. Set to True when searching private repositories; False searches all of GitHub and produces large noisy result sets.

input.description: Request schema for finding pull requests with AI-friendly parameters.

capabilities.description: AI-optimized repository search with smart filtering by language, stars, topics, and ownership. Builds intelligent search queries and returns clean, actionable repository data. Check `incomplete_results` in the response — when true, results are non-exhaustive. Search endpoints are rate-limited to ~30 requests/minute (vs. 5000/hour for general REST); apply backoff on 403/429. Total results are capped at ~1000 per query regardless of pagination.

page.description: Page number of results to fetch.

owner.description: Filter by specific user or organization. Do NOT use this parameter if your 'query' already contains 'user:', 'org:', or 'repo:' qualifiers - they will conflict. Use either 'owner' parameter OR search qualifiers in 'query', not both.

query.description: Search query for repository name, description, or README content. Accepts both 'query' and 'q' as parameter names. Supports OR operator for alternatives (e.g., 'bug OR error'). Multi-word phrases in OR expressions are automatically quoted. GitHub limits OR expressions to 6 terms maximum; queries exceeding this limit are truncated. If using GitHub qualifiers like 'repo:', 'user:', or 'org:', they must be properly formatted (e.g., 'repo:owner/name', 'user:username', 'org:orgname').

archived.description: Filter by archived status. None means include both.

per_page.description: Number of results per page (maximum 100). GitHub caps total results at ~1000 per query; for exhaustive searches, split by `language`, `topic`, `min_stars`/`max_stars`, or `owner`.

max_stars.description: Maximum number of stars the repository should have.

min_forks.description: Minimum number of forks the repository should have.

min_stars.description: Minimum number of stars the repository should have.

fork_filter.description: How to handle forks: 'include' (include forks), 'exclude' (exclude forks), 'only' (only forks).

response_detail.description: Level of detail in the response. 'minimal' (default) returns an optimized response for AI agents. 'full' returns the complete GitHub API response.

for_authenticated_user.description: Search only in repositories accessible to the authenticated user (including private repos). Requires token scopes `repo`/`read:org`; sparse results compared to GitHub UI typically indicate insufficient token scopes.

capabilities.description: Lists repositories accessible to the authenticated user based on visibility, affiliation, and type filters. Returns repositories owned by the user, those they collaborate on, or those accessible through organization membership. Use this action when you need to retrieve a comprehensive list of repositories the authenticated user can access, with options to filter by visibility (public/private), affiliation (owner/collaborator/organization), or type. Supports pagination for large result sets.

page.description: Page number of results to fetch.

sort.description: The property to sort the results by.

type.description: Limit results to repositories of the specified type. Note: Using 'type' with 'visibility' or 'affiliation' will cause a 422 error. Use either 'type' OR 'visibility'/'affiliation', not both.

since.description: Only show repositories updated after the given time. This is a timestamp in ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.

before.description: Only show repositories updated before the given time. This is a timestamp in ISO 8601 format: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ.

per_page.description: Number of results per page (maximum 100).

direction.description: The order to sort by. Default: asc when using full_name, otherwise desc.

visibility.description: Limit results to repositories with the specified visibility (all, public, or private).

affiliation.description: Comma-separated list of values defining which repositories to include: 'owner' (repositories owned by the authenticated user), 'collaborator' (repositories where the user is a collaborator), 'organization_member' (repositories accessible through organization membership). When not specified, defaults to 'owner,collaborator,organization_member'.

input.description: Request schema for listing repositories for the authenticated user.

capabilities.description: Lists issues (including pull requests) from a GitHub repository. Requires BOTH 'owner' AND 'repo' parameters (e.g., owner='octocat', repo='Hello-World' for github.com/octocat/Hello-World).

page.description: Page number for the set of results. Refer to GitHub's REST API documentation for pagination details.

repo.description: REQUIRED. The name of the repository (without .git extension). For 'octocat/Hello-World', repo is 'Hello-World'. Not case-sensitive. Must be provided together with 'owner'.

sort.description: The field to sort the results by.

type.description: Filter issues by type name. Use '*' for issues with any type, 'none' for issues without a type, or specify a type name.

owner.description: REQUIRED. The GitHub account owner (user or organization) of the repository. For 'octocat/Hello-World', owner is 'octocat'. Not case-sensitive. Must be provided together with 'repo'.

since.description: Filters issues to include only those updated at or after the specified time. This should be a timestamp in ISO 8601 format (e.g., `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`).

state.description: Filters issues based on their state.

labels.description: A comma-separated list of label names to filter issues by. Example: 'bug,ui,@high'.

creator.description: Filter issues by the username of the user who created the issue.

assignee.description: Filter issues by assignee's username. Use 'none' for issues with no assignee, or '*' for issues assigned to any user.

per_page.description: Number of results per page (max 100). Default is 30, which matches GitHub's API default. Refer to GitHub's REST API documentation for pagination details.

mentioned.description: Filter issues by a user mentioned in the issue's description or comments. Provide the username.

milestone.description: Filter issues by milestone. Provide the milestone `number` as a string, '*' for issues with any milestone, or 'none' for issues without a milestone.

input.description: Request parameters for listing issues from a GitHub repository. IMPORTANT: GitHub repositories are identified by BOTH 'owner' AND 'repo'. For example, to list issues from 'https://github.com/octocat/Hello-World': - owner = 'octocat' (the account/organization name) - repo = 'Hello-World' (the repository name) You MUST provide both 'owner' and 'repo' - providing only 'repo' will fail.
